title: Deterministic Uniform Inter-Arrival Schedule in Load Generator
pattern: A load generator issues requests at perfectly uniform intervals (`t0, t0 + dt, t0 + 2dt, ...`) when modelling production traffic.
why_bad: Real arrivals are bursty (Poisson or heavier-tailed). Evenly spaced requests rarely overlap, so queueing contention that production bursts create never happens in the test, and latency at a given utilization looks far better than it will be.
detection: A load schedule computed with a constant `Duration` between arrivals, with no sampling from a random inter-arrival distribution (exponential, Pareto) or replay of recorded traffic, in a benchmark whose results are used to predict production latency.
counterexample: Micro-benchmarks isolating a single component's service time where deterministic spacing is deliberate, and tests reproducing a known periodic producer.
source: Brendan Gregg, *Systems Performance* (2013), Ch. 8, §8.7, p. 385; Ch. 12, §12.3, p. 593.
